Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our RFP packet for the next-phase evaluation (short-listing). The security and legal teams asked for detailed answers on the following high-level areas:

- Encryption at rest: key management model, BYOK support, HSM attestations
- Encryption in transit: TLS versions, mutual TLS support for private deploys
- PHI routing & segregation: whether PHI ever leaves Healthex's VPC or is processed in shared pools

Also list any open items that would require product changes or legal exceptions so procurement can evaluate risk.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP: PHI handling, encryption, and BAA — initial questionnaire

Hi team,

I reviewed Healthex's questionnaire and prepared a technical pack. High-level answers below (I'll attach the evidence PDF + diagram):

- Encryption at rest:
  - All hosted data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Customer keys are supported via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with envelope encryption.
  - For Dedicated and Private deployments we support BYOK where customer-managed keys are used and we never persist raw keys. HSM-backed key wrapping is available upon request (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 as an option for Private installs).

- Encryption in transit:
  - All network traffic is TLS 1.2+; we default to TLS 1.3 where supported.
  - Private deployments and Dedicated endpoints can be configured with mutual TLS for customer mTLS authentication.

- PHI routing & segregation:
  - Hosted (multi-tenant) customers are logically isolated by tenancy. PHI is processed on tenancy-specific namespaces but may be scheduled on shared GPU pools unless customer purchases Dedicated/Private where physical isolation is enforced.
  - For customers that require PHI to remain in their VPC, our Private deployment variant supports a customer-controlled data plane (requests never egress to Redwood-hosted pools).

- Auditability & logs:
  - We provide request-level logging (timestamps, route/model, token counts, request/response hashes — not full outputs by default).
  - Audit logs can be exported to the customer's logging endpoint (S3/Cloud Storage/CloudWatch) with configurable retention. We retain operator logs for 90 days by default; can extend under contract.

- Data residency & deletion:
  - We support region pinning for data and model inference.
  - Deletion: we expose a deletion API and a purge workflow; for Private deployments deletion is handled by customer-controlled storage. For hosted customers we provide deletion receipts and a proof bundle (manifest + storage tombstone) — however, complete immutable forensic proof can be limited by underlying cloud provider retention policies.

Open/engineering items to flag:
- Live-request sampling for full response archival is off by default. If Healthex requires full-response capture for every request we need to enable capture and confirm retention/secure storage; this impacts cost and operational controls.
- FIPS/HSM provisioning for hosted multi-tenant customers: currently available for Private/Dedicated; hosted BYOK with HSM attestation would require a separate provisioning timeline.

I'm attaching: RedwOOD_security_evidence_summary.pdf (controls mapping + SOC2 pointer), redwood_network_diagram.png (data flow showing Private vs Hosted), and a sample audit export manifest.

- Monica
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_security_evidence_summary.pdf, redwood_network_diagram.png

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-16 11:14 PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP: PHI handling, encryption, and BAA — initial questionnaire

Team,

I reviewed Healthex's BAA expectations and prepared a draft redline. Key negotiation points:

- Deletion & backup windows: we can commit to deletion workflows and receipts; cannot guarantee irrevocable scrub of provider-level backups within 24 hours due to cloud backup retention — recommend a 30-day backup retention carve-out in the BAA.
- Indemnity: standard mutual indemnities are acceptable; Healthex's ask for unlimited indemnity for third-party claims tied to PHI is not acceptable — propose cap to contracted fees with carve-outs for gross negligence.
- Subprocessors: we will list cloud provider subprocessors and will agree to notify changes; Healthex requests approval rights — propose a 30-day notice and right to terminate under material change.
- Audit rights: we accept audit requests via third-party assessor annually, with reasonable notice and scoped to controls relevant to PHI processing.

I've attached a tracked redline: BAA_redline_Healthex_2027.docx. If Healthex requires certain language for deletion proof beyond our current mechanisms, we'll need legal approval and possibly a product-side change.

Markus
Markus Klein
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BAA_redline_Healthex_2027.docx

Hi Sarah — thanks for the RFP and timeline. Attached is our consolidated response bundle and supporting evidence (see list below). We've tried to be as explicit as possible and have flagged open items where we need mutual agreement or product/legal exceptions.

Summary of attachments:
- Consolidated_RFP_Response_Healthex.pdf — narrative answers to each questionnaire item (encryption, routing, auditability, retention).
- Redwood_security_evidence_summary.pdf — controls mapping and pointer to SOC2 report excerpts.
- redwood_network_diagram.png — infrastructure diagram (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- BAA_redline_Healthex_2027.docx — tracked changes with our proposed language.

Open items we flagged for your review:
1) Full-response archival: off by default. If Healthex requires capture of full model outputs for all requests we need to enable capture and agree on retention/secure storage costs.
2) HSM attestation for hosted tenancy: HSM-backed key attestations are supported in Private deployments; for hosted BYOK with HSM attestation this would require a provisioning project and lead time.
3) Backup retention carve-out: we proposed a 30-day backup carve-out in the BAA for provider-level backups.

Next steps we propose:
- Please review the attached BAA redline and mark any non-starters.
- If the team wants a technical walkthrough, Monica can run a 45-min session this week and show the Private/Dedicated architecture and evidence export flows.
- If Healthex is comfortable, we can send a DocuSign link for the proposed BAA and follow with a Dedicated trial for validation.

Internal reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Healthex+-+RFP+HX-2027-046
